<role>
You check one property (signal) of a product-feedback opportunity for Keelwater, a claims-handling software company. You do not rewrite anything.
</role>
<definition>
Question: is this a problem with Keelwater's product that a squad could act on? Pass means yes.
Fail if the cause is outside the product (pricing, contracts, the customer's own IT, staffing), if a help article would have answered it, or if it is praise.
A feature request or a described workaround is signal.
The evidence is the title, the problem statement and up to 12 customer quotes with route and date.
</definition>
<evidence>
{
 "title": "Garage estimates misclassified as correspondence",
 "problem_statement": "Handlers must manually reclassify garage estimates that are incorrectly filed as correspondence, leading to delays and missed evidence. This error undermines claim accuracy because critical documents are overlooked during processing.",
 "quotes": [
  {
   "quote": "Garage estimates keep landing in correspondence — we have to manually recategorise them, and sometimes evidence gets missed because of it. The incorrect file type assignment is causing real delays and oversight risks.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-27T09:02:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "garage estimates keep landing in correspondence — we have to manually recategorise them, and sometimes evidence gets missed because of it.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-27T09:02:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "Handlers are spending too much time fixing the incorrect file type assignments — we need a better way to classify garage estimates so we don’t miss critical evidence during claims processing.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-27T09:02:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "We’re still wrestling with the wrong document category issue — garage estimates keep landing in Correspondence, and our handlers have to manually move them, which risks missing critical evidence.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-11T12:56:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "Also, every time we upload a garage estimate, it lands in correspondence — it’s a wrong document category and handlers keep missing key evidence because of it.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-18T08:15:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "Uploaded documents are sometimes misfiled — garage estimates get dumped into correspondence, forcing handlers to manually reassign them, and that’s where evidence can slip through the cracks because of ... file type assignment.",
   "route": "onboarding",
   "date": "2026-10-12T08:59:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "handlers are wasting time fixing incorrect file type assignments, and it’s impacting claim accuracy",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-27T09:02:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "garage estimates keep landing in Correspondence, and our handlers have to manually move them, which risks missing critical evidence",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-11T12:56:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "when evidence gets misfiled, it can slip through the cracks... Every time a garage estimate gets dumped into correspondence, someone has to manually fix it — and sometimes the wrong document category means evidence gets overlooked entirely.",
   "route": "account_management",
   "date": "2026-09-11T14:49:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "Every time we upload a garage estimate, it lands in correspondence — it’s a wrong document category and handlers keep missing key evidence because of it, which delays claims resolution.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-18T08:15:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "when we upload garage estimates, they’re landing in the wrong document category—like under Correspondence—and we’re having to manually move them, which risks things slipping through the cracks... they’re being auto-sorted into the wrong document category, which forces us to manually reassign them — and sometimes that leads to important evidence being missed during review.",
   "route": "onboarding",
   "date": "2026-10-06T14:24:00+00:00"
  }
 ]
}
</evidence>
<task>
Write a critique of 2-5 sentences naming the claim, quote or item you checked and what you found. Then give the verdict. If any single item fails, the verdict is fail.
</task>
<output>
JSON only: {"critique": string, "verdict": "pass" | "fail"}
</output>

response.content: {"critique": "The claim is that Keelwater's document classification incorrectly files garage estimates as correspondence, forcing manual reclassification and risking missed evidence. Multiple quotes across support, onboarding, and account_management routes (Sept–Oct 2026) consistently describe the same in-product misclassification and workaround, indicating a product behavior a squad could address. No quote attributes the cause to pricing, contracts, customer IT, or staffing, and none is praise or answered by a help article.","verdict": "pass"}
